As stated in this corrigendum, as well as in the Prosecution's submission of the 15th of February, 2008, the opportunistic killing incidents listed at paragraphs 31.1(b) and (c) of the indictment are not proven. Therefore, the only opportunistic killings charged at Potocari are the nine bodies found near the UN compound on the Budak side of the main road, which is paragraph 31.1(a), and the summary execution of one man near the White House, which is paragraph 31.1(d). Although the indictment refers to the nine men being killed on the 12th of July, the evidence in the case has shown that nine men were killed on the 13th of July at that location. Also, the opportunistic killing incident near the Kravica supermarket listed at paragraph 31.3 of the indictment include the allegation that, I quote: "A VRS or MUP soldier placed his rifle barrel into the mouth of a Bosnian Muslim prisoner and summarily executed the man." As stated in the corrigendum, there is insufficient evidence to prove that this man was killed. However, as detailed in the Prosecution's final brief, the other violence and killings near the Kravica supermarket have been proven. A number of Defence briefs assert that individual accused did not know about the opportunistic killing incidents that actually occurred and did not contribute to those incidents. I'm referring, for example, to the Beara final brief at paragraphs 487 to 490, the Miletic final brief at paragraphs 497 and 498, the Nikolic final brief at paragraphs 1309 to 1312, and the Pandurevic final brief at page 228. However, these elements are not relevant to a JCE 3 analysis. What the Prosecution has to prove is that the crimes occurred, that such crimes were the natural and foreseeable consequences of carrying out the JCEs, and that the accused JCE members willingly took that risk. Based on this framework, many of the points raised in the Defence briefs, supposedly concerning liability for opportunistic killings, in fact concern matters entirely outside the scope of the relevant analysis. I want to make two brief points as to the applicable law. The first is the degree of foreseeability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, before you do so, when referring to opportunistic killings, you dealt with the ones in Potocari or related to Potocari and the ones related to Kravica supermarket or Kravica. You haven't said anything about the ones alleged to have taken place in Bratunac and Petkovci. Do you have a position on those?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: They -- it's the Prosecution's position that they are proven and the charges are left untouched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I simply didn't mention them, Your Honour, because we weren't making any alterations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: As to the applicable law, Your Honours, then the first point is the degree of foreseeability, the Appeals Chamber has affirmed in a 25th of June, 2009 decision in the Karadzic case that, I quote: "Plotted on a spectrum of likelihood, the JCE 3 mens rea standard does not require an understanding that a deviatory crime would probably be committed. It does, however, require that the possibility a crime could be committed is sufficiently substantial has to be foreseeable to an accused. Second is the fact that the Appeals Chamber has held that an accused JCE member can be guilty of specific intent crimes which are foreseeable consequences of the JCE, and that's an Appeals Chamber decision from Brdjanin on interlocutory appeal dated the 19th of March, 2004, and this jurisprudence is on point and it applies to the crimes charged in this case. As regards foreseeability, the Gvero final brief argues at paragraph 48 that, I quote: "It is the Defence position that as these crimes were, in fact, carried out for reasons of personal revenge, it would have been completely impossible for Milan Gvero to foresee their commission, as they bore no relationship whatsoever to the forcible transfer operation." Your Honours, the evidence supports entirely the opposite conclusion. The circumstances in which the forcible removal JCE and the murder JCE took place was such that spontaneous killings or revenge killings were objectively foreseeable as possible consequences of those operations. I won't go into great detail in describing this, but as explained throughout the case, retaliatory violence had occurred in and around the Srebrenica enclave from 1992 onwards. Furthermore, violence towards the Srebrenica Muslims was clearly foreseeable as part of the policy to ethnically cleanse areas claimed as Bosnian Serb land, including the Drina River Valley, and particularly was foreseeable in light of the brutal history of the war. As well as having to be objectively foreseeable, there is also a subjective requirement, that the crimes were foreseeable to each accused. However, as all of the accused were officers of the armed forces of Republika Srpska throughout the war, there can be no suggestion that any one of them lacked the necessary knowledge of the historical build-up, hatred, and policy of ethnic cleansing that existed prior to July 1995 such that they could not foresee that serious violence, including murder, might result from the criminal plan to rid the enclaves of their Muslim population. As regards what distinguishes opportunistic killings from the organised mass killings of July 1995, the indictment makes this clear at paragraph 83, a part of which reads as follows: "The term 'opportunistic' is used in this indictment to describe killings and other criminal acts carried out by individual soldiers, acting on their own, likely without orders from superior officers." So these killings were not part of the planned sequence of events of the murder JCE. They took place at locations other than the chosen execution sites and for reasons other than military orders. They represent the level of attendant violence that was accepted by the JCE members as the possible consequence of the plan to rid Srebrenica of its Muslim population. Each of the charged incidents fits this characterisation. The killings in Potocari, Bratunac, near the Kravica supermarket, and at the Petkovci school occurred at locations where they risked discovery by DutchBat or by uninvolved members of the local population. Furthermore, they did not involve the killing of all the Muslim men who were at those locations, indicating that they were carried out either as spontaneous acts of violence or as acts of targeted revenge. Even after the murder operation started, these killings occurred in a way that was clearly opportunistic and foreseeable in a way that the vast and organised mass killings were not foreseeable as a consequence of the forcible removal JCE. That is the distinction. That is why the forcible removal JCE members are liable for these killings, but not the mass executions. Next, I'd like to address certain factual allegations specifically concerning the nine men killed near Potocari. The Gvero final brief makes a number of arguments about these victims, with the following proposed as reasonable possibilities: First, and this is at paragraphs 75 and 76 of the Gvero brief, it is argued that the nine bodies were found in the Jaglici and Susnjari area, where the Muslim men formed the column and set off towards Tuzla on the evening of the 11th of July, suggesting that the victims could have been competent members of the column and, I quote: "... and that they may have perished as a result of earlier mutual conflicts or acts of personal revenge committed by individuals within the column." Second, it is argued that the nine men may have been killed by retreating Bosnian Muslim fighters who were seen on the 11th of July, but who had left for the woods by 12th of July, and that's at paragraph 77 of the Gvero brief. Third, it's argued that the nine men may have been killed by an individual seen by Major Rutten fleeing the scene, and that's at paragraph 74 of the Gvero brief. And, fourth, the fact that identification documents were found near the bodies is argued to be inconsistent with the VRS force's practice of confiscating prisoners' IDs immediately, suggesting that the nine men may not have been killed by VRS forces. And that's paragraph 78 of the Gvero brief. These supposed reasonable doubts are, first of all, based on inaccurate foundations. It may just be a simple error, but the bodies were found only a few hundred metres from the main road in Potocari, not in the Jaglici and Susnjari area, and those villages are more than five kilometres away from Potocari, over the hills. I don't need to show you this in court, but it can be seen, for example, on the Krivaja 95 map, which is P01463. So it's not correct to say that they were found in the area where the Muslim men gathered before leaving in the column. Second, it's clear that the nine men were killed only shortly before Major Rutten and Lieutenant Koster saw them on the 13th of July, and Rutten's Krstic testimony, and this is at page 2140, he said the following when he saw the bodies -- he said the following of when he saw the bodies, and I quote: "The blood was still running. There were no flies on them. It was very warm that day, so you could easily say that it hadn't been long ago that they were shot." When you compare this with other evidence about how quickly bodies deteriorated in the heat, it's clear that those nine men were killed on the morning of the 13th of July. For comparison, Muslim column member PW-116, in his witness statement, which is Exhibit P02206, described how he came across bodies in the hills above Kravica and Sandici on the 13th of July, which cannot have been there for more than a day, since the column only set off on the night of the 11th of July from Jaglici and Susnjari and would have passed through that area on the 12th of July. He said, and I quote: "It was very hot, and flies came to the bodies. The smell was terrible. I could not look at the bodies anymore." In that kind of heat, Rutten could not have seen the bodies very long after they were killed. In response to the other suggested scenarios put forward in the Gvero brief, the first point is that it is not a reasonable possibility that Muslim men in civilian clothes, who were alive within a few hundred metres of the main Potocari road on the morning of the 13th of July, were members of the Muslim column or had been killed by the men in the column or by retreating Muslim fighters fleeing to join the column. That group had gathered far away and was long gone by that time. The next supposedly reasonable scenario, for the Muslim man in civilian clothes seen fleeing from the general area might have killed the nine men, is again simply not credible. It is not reasonable that a killer would stay around at the murder scene long enough to be seen fleeing from the general area when the DutchBat officers, responding to rumours, arrived to investigate. Anyway, the only Muslim men in Potocari on the 13th of July were those in the crowd of refugees, and they had no motivation and were not in a position to carry out mass murders of other Muslim men. Lastly, it is not reasonable to draw any conclusion, based on the presence of the victims' identification documents near the bodies, that the murderers may have been -- may not have been members of the Bosnian Serb forces. Clearly, not all Muslim men had their IDs taken away when they were captured or separated by VRS or MUP soldiers, and there are plenty of cases of IDs being found in the mass graves. Gvero's arguments that the nine men may have been killed by fellow Muslims are predicated on they're having been killed when there were still Muslim fighters in the Potocari area. The only evidence that could possibly suggest this is that of Witness PW-114, who saw nine or ten bodies on what he said was the 12th of July, but he also insisted that it was the second day of the transport of the Muslim population out of Potocari, which of course was the 13th of July. Furthermore, PW-114 testified that he didn't know when the men had been killed, but on cross-examination answered the question, and I quote: "Q. Can you tell us if you know when these people were killed? "A. No, I don't know the time. I was there at noon, so it must be maybe on the 11th or on the 12th in the morning." And that's at transcript reference 3164. Either PW-114 saw different bodies from those seen by Rutten and Koster, or he saw the bodies on the 13th of July. The obvious conclusion is that all three witnesses saw the same bodies on the same day. This is clear both from their similar testimonies and from the fact that only nine bodies have been exhumed from the field just by the stream where the bodies were seen. And if you look at Exhibit P03897, this shows clearly how all three eye-witnesses recall seeing bodies within a few metres of where nine bodies were subsequently exhumed. In these circumstances, PW-114's failure to resolve the inconsistency of seeing the bodies on the 12th of July, but at the same time on the second day of the transportations, doesn't matter. It is clear that the bodies of nine men were found on the 13th, and those men were killed on the 13th. However, even if they had been killed on the 12th of July, there is no way that these men could have been killed by mysterious Muslims carrying out internal revenge killings within only a few hundred metres of a huge VRS and MUP presence in Potocari on the 12th and 13th of July, as seen, for example, on the trial video which is Exhibit P02047. Next, I want to address an argument raised in the Pandurevic final brief, which at page 210 argues that, I quote: "The indictment alleges also that the crime of persecution was a necessary and foreseeable consequence of the plan to transfer the population." The Defence frankly wonder whether this was a mistake in the indictment's drafting. The particulars of paragraph 48 of the indictment cannot properly be characterised as individual criminal acts when it actually describes the whole alleged murder and forcible transfer operations. Paragraph 83 of the indictment states that it was foreseeable to the accused, I quote: "... that individual criminal acts, such as individual opportunistic killings and persecutory acts, as described in paragraphs 31 and 48 of this indictment, would be carried out by Serb forces during the joint criminal enterprise to forcibly transfer and deport the populations of the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves." Clearly, in addition to the opportunistic killings, points 48(b), (c) and (d) are the relevant persecutory acts for consideration as foreseeable crimes pursuant to JCE 3, 48(b) being the cruel and inhumane treatment of Bosnian Muslim civilians, including murder and severe beatings at Potocari and in detention facilities in Bratunac and Zvornik, 48(c) being the terrorising of Bosnian Muslim civilians in Srebrenica and at Potocari, and 48(d) being the destruction of personal property and effects belonging to the Bosnian Muslims. These crimes of persecution were the natural and foreseeable consequences of the forcible removal JCE, irrespective of their nature as crimes against humanity. The "Chapeau" requirements for such crimes are fulfilled by the nature of the attack on Srebrenica as a widespread and systematic attack against the civilian population and because the persecutory acts, themselves, had a sufficient nexus with that attack since they were carried out by members of the same attacking forces and were directed against members of the same population. Once those elements are proven, the remaining question is whether the actual persecutory acts were foreseeable, for the reasons that I've already explained; namely, the violence and hatred against the Muslims and specifically against the Srebrenica Muslims, they were indeed foreseeable. Finally, I want to reiterate what Mr. Mitchell has already said, that the Muslim men who were taken to the Zvornik area did not lose their status as victims of the forcible transfer operation just because at some point they also became the intended victims of the murder operation. The men who were separated in Potocari or captured from the fleeing column were transported away from the Srebrenica enclave. The possibility of opportunistic crimes being committed against these men, when they were moved through Bratunac and through locations in the Zvornik area, was foreseeable to the members of the forcible removal JCE, just as were the crimes committed against Muslims in the crowd at Potocari, such as the man shot near the White House or the nine men killed near the stream towards Budak. Your Honours, I have a very brief further submission concerning reburials, and this is simply to address questions raised in the Nikolic final brief concerning the inclusion of the reburials in the indictment. Again, I'm not going to deal with the factual details or the nature of the accuseds' participation in the operation. Those are covered in the Prosecution's final brief starting at page 311 as well as in the sections concerning the individual accused. I will just deal with the arguments raised in the section of the Nikolic brief entitled "The Alleged Reburial Operation has no Purpose," which is at paragraphs 260 to 274. The conclusion of this section at paragraph 274 states: "For all intents and purposes, the inclusion of the alleged reburial operation into the indictment serves no apparent goal. The Defence submits that the Trial Chamber must disregard it as either: (a), a component of the alleged general side; (b), reasonably foreseeable consequence of the alleged murder operation; (c), a crime in and of itself; and (d), ex post facto aiding and abetting the alleged murder operation." The conclusion that a reburial operation is irrelevant is wrong, and I want to highlight the reasons why the reburial operation is included in the indictment, since it was a major planned military undertaking, and it should inform the Trial Chamber's deliberations concerning the murder JCE. The indictment at paragraph 32 indeed states that, and I quote: "The reburial operation was a natural and foreseeable consequence of the execution and original burial plan conceived by the joint criminal enterprise." This characterisation reflects the Prosecution's evidence that the reburials were foreseeable to the members of the murder JCE in July 1995. It was foreseeable from the outset of the murder JCE that the initial steps taken to conceal the crimes in July 1995 might not be sufficient because the killings and burials were so extensive and so hastily organised. That such crimes could not be concealed so easily was borne out by what actually occurred. The disappearance of thousands of Muslim men from Srebrenica quickly became well known, and the burials of many of the victims were carried out hurriedly and involved civilian as well as military personnel. The Trial Chamber should, for example, consider the testimony of Witnesses PW-161, PW-170, and PW-104. Because the killings and burials were not well concealed, it was foreseeable that further steps might be needed to hide the crimes. In any event, this foreseeability is not a necessary element to establish the guilt of the accused under any of the modes of liability charged, since all five accused charged with genocide both joined and contributed to the JCE in July 1995, before the reburial operation started. Those who were involved in the reburial operation, in other words, all five, other than Borovcanin, further contributed to the crimes by their involvement in the reburials at a later stage. As well as taking into account the reburial operation when considering the liability of the individual accused, the operation is also hugely significant as an act of concealment, which confirms the knowledge and intent of the JCE members as participants of a massive criminal enterprise to murder the Muslim men of Srebrenica. Finally, as the Trial Chamber will hear from Ms. Soljan, the destruction of the Muslim women and children was a component of the genocide, and the reburials clearly were an element which contributed to the inability of the surviving Muslim population to recover from the loss of their men, since afterwards it would be even more difficult to locate, identify, mourn, and come to terms with the fate of their murdered fathers, brothers, husbands, and sons. Those are my submissions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, Counsel, good afternoon. The Prosecution has proven beyond a reasonable doubt that the five accused, Vinko Pandurevic, Ljubomir Borovcanin, Ljubisa Beara, Vujadin Popovic, and Drago Nikolic, are responsible for genocide committed against the Bosnian Muslim population of Eastern Bosnia, as charged in paragraphs 26 to 33 of the indictment. It has proven that with a goal of destroying the Bosnian Muslim population of Eastern Bosnia, the VRS and RS MUP forces carried out the following genocidal acts enumerated in Article 4(2), (A) through (D) of the Statute: (a), they killed over 7.000 Bosnian Muslim men from Srebrenica; (b), they caused serious bodily or mental harm to both the male and female members of the Bosnian Muslim population of Srebrenica and Zepa; (c), they created conditions contributing to the physical destruction of the Bosnian Muslim population of Srebrenica and Zepa; and, (d), they contributed to the failure of the Muslim population of Srebrenica and Zepa to live and reproduce normally. I shall briefly address two issues related to the genocide account. First, I will address some of the factual issues raised by the Defence concerning the number of Srebrenica victims, more specifically the number of persons killed, as charged in paragraphs 26(a) and paragraphs 27 to 32 of the indictment. After that, I shall briefly speak about the destruction of the Muslim population of Eastern Bosnia, focusing in particular on the destruction of women and children caused by the separations of the men at Potocari, their subsequent murder, as well as by the forcible transfers from the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, as charged in paragraph 26(b) and paragraph 33 of the indictment. With respect to the first issue, Your Honours, the number of Srebrenica victims, the Defence argues that anywhere from 1.500 to 3.000 Srebrenica persons died in legitimate combat, as well as a result of land-mines, suicides, or friendly-fires. You can find references to this in Popovic final brief paragraph 708 and 886; the Beara final brief, paragraphs 584 and 586; and the Nikolic final brief at paragraph 1493. The Defence also argues that the figure 3.000 is indicative of the total number of missing persons from Srebrenica, and that, and I quote: "... not in excess of 2.000 to 3.000 victims were killed in Srebrenica." This is from the Nikolic final brief at paragraph 1494. Evidence, however, shows that the Defence figures wildly underestimate the number of Srebrenica victims. First of all, evidence shows that almost 8.000 persons from Srebrenica are missing. Based on a rigorous demographic analysis, the minimal number of Srebrenica missing persons was determined to be 7.661. As you will recall from Mr. Brunborg's 2000 report on the number of missing and dead from Srebrenica, and this is Exhibit P571, this is a conservative number. In some cases, entire families went missing, leaving no surviving family member to register the information with the ICRC. This minimum demographic figure was revised to 7.826 Srebrenica missing persons in January 2008, when the list was cross-referenced with the then current ICMP DNA matching data. This would have been Exhibit P3002, the October 2007 ICM -- ICMP update, and is also reflected in Exhibit P3159, which was the then report on the ICMP's DNA identifications. Based on ICMP's recent 10 April 2009 Srebrenica tracking chart, Exhibit P4500, the number of persons reported to ICMP as missing from Srebrenica, and as represented by donor relative blood samples, is 7.789, a figure very close to demographic accounting, but obtained independently of the ICRC. I note that the Nikolic Defence, at paragraph 1469 of its brief, incorrectly states that, I quote: "The 2009 ICMP update is based on information provided by the family of the missing person to the ICRC." Dr. Parsons, in fact, testified that information regarding individuals reported missing regarding any event in Bosnia came directly to the ICMP from the family members. So to quote: "To associate it with Srebrenica, that would have been information that the family provided to us." Reference page 20873 of the transcript. Dr. Parsons also explained that ICMP's expert interview teams meet with families, obtain genetic blood samples, properly record all relevant information, including the date and place of disappearance of missing persons, which are then nominally set as 11 July 1995 and as either Potocari or forest, which are then placed on the match report and update for purposes of keeping track of the ICMP Srebrenica cases in an internally-consistent manner. The reference to this is at 20875 to 20876. In short, the ICMP information is based on information and blood samples provided by family members to the ICMP, not the ICRC. Now, of the almost 8.000 Srebrenica persons reported missing, we have evidence that approximately 2.000 of those persons were separated at Potocari. We also have evidence that at least 5.000 of them were captured or surrendered from the column along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, and, finally, that at least 648 of these individuals identified from surface remains were killed along the column route. They were not only in combat. Let's take a closer look at these figures. With respect to the evidence that shows approximately 2.000 men separated at Potocari, first of all, we have the demographic evidence which shows that 2.070 individuals were reported missing from Potocari in the month of July 1995. We see this at Exhibit P2413, which is the report from 2003. In our final brief at paragraph 496, the dates of disappearance from men reported missing from Potocari were narrowed to just 10 to 13 July, and the number was still 2.003. Currently, 1443 individuals reported by the ICRC as missing from Potocari had been identified through DNA. This can be verified by comparing the most recent ICMP update, Exhibit P4494 with the previously listed exhibit, P3159A, which is the 2007 progress report on ICMP's identifications, which also contains the date on ICRC dates and place of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: That would be 1.443. The vast majority of these individuals can be found in the primary and secondary graves related to all the major executions and execution sites, including Kravica, Orahovac, Petkovci Dam, Kozluk, and Branjevo Farm, as well as Pilica. It can also be found in the primary undisturbed graves, such as Bisina, Nova Kasaba, Konjevic Polje, and others. In addition, some of these individuals reported as having gone missing from Potocari have been identified from surface remains. As an example, 12 of the 14 individuals identified via DNA from the Kozluk surface remains, which we can find in Confidential Annex D to the Dusan Janc report, this is Exhibit number P4491, they were found -- and the most reasonable inference is that they were separated at Potocari. This specifically contradicts the Defence arguments by the Beara Defence at paragraph 635, as well as the Popovic Defence argument as paragraph 755, that the Kozluk surface remains are legitimate combat casualties of a battle taking place in the area. Second, of almost 8.000 persons reported missing, at least 5.000 were captured along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. While the evidence concerning the movement of the column, the surrenders, the captures, is dealt with in greater detail in the Prosecution final brief at paragraphs 518 through 544, I'd like to make just a few basic points in order to respond to Defence arguments. Evidence has shown that approximately 15.000 Muslim civilians and ABiH 28th Division soldiers gathered near the village of Jaglici and Susnjari on the eve of 11 July and set out westwards in a column towards the Muslim-held territory. Now, I'm emphasising the word "westward" in order to address an entirely unsupported argument at paragraph 613 of the Beara Defence final brief, namely, that the column -- and I quote: "... would have very likely taken soldiers through the area of Ravnice, where the column may have been attacked or ambushed." Now, this argument is a part of Beara's broader argument, that bodies found in the Glogova, Ravnice, and Zeleni Jadar graves got there as a result of legitimate combat. There is no evidence whatsoever in the record that the column ever went in such a convoluted north-eastern direction in order to reach the Konjevic Polje intersection which is squarely to the west on their way north-east to Tuzla. We only need to take a look at the map showing the movement of the column, which is Exhibit P2110, in order to see that the column went from Susnjari and Jaglici through the so-called Pobudje area, south of Bratunac, well south of Glogova and Ravnice graves, and moving westward in the hills south of the Bratunac and Konjevic Polje road towards the Konjevic Polje intersection. For further reference, you can also see Exhibit P04524, which was the map of connections from primary to secondary graves based on DNA and forensic evidence. Evidence shows that as many as 6.000 men and boys from the column were captured or surrendered along the road. An intercepted conversation at 530 hours -- 1730 hours on July 13th, which is Exhibit P1143A, shows that the Bosnian Serbs had captured approximately 6.000 Muslim men along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road that day. It tells us that approximately 1.500 to 2.000 men were detained at three major sites; Nova Kasaba, Konjevic Polje, Sandici Meadow. And we know that survivors, such as PW-116, PW-113, PW-111, who were captured and placed at Nova Kasaba or Sandici Meadow corroborate those numbers. Demographic evidence shows that at least 4.600 individuals were reported as missing from the area along the route of the column between Jaglici and Susnjari and Konjevic Polje. Roughly, this number includes 1.085 men reported as missing from the forest, 2.338 men reported as missing from Konjevic Polje, Kravica, or Kamenica, and approximately 1.200 persons reported as missing from smaller locations in the Pobudje area along the route of the column prior to the Konjevic Polje crossing. We can see this at exhibits P2413, the demographic report specifically at ERN 0501-6201, as well as Exhibit P3159A, the 2007 progress report. Now, what do we know about the Muslim men who were captured or surrendered from the forest and various locations? We will see that the vast majority of these individuals have been identified in the primary and secondary mass graves related to all the major executions and execution sites, including Kravica, Orahovac, Petkovci Dam, Kozluk, Branjevo Farm, and Pilica, as well as in primary undisturbed graves such as Trnovo, Bisina, Nova Kasaba, Konjevic Polje. Now, we know that in addition to the approximately 2.000 men who were separated in Potocari, as well as at least 5.000 men who surrendered or were captured along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, there are 648 individuals whose remains have been identified at the surface, primarily along the route of the column. Before discussing these individuals, let's just briefly look at the DNA evidence concerning the numbers of individuals in mass graves. If I may, Your Honours, could I take the break now and we'll continue immediately thereafter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, I think that's perfect. We'll resume in 25 minutes' time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As of 31 January, 6.006 individuals from Srebrenica have been identified via DNA analysis by the ICMP. The exhibit for this is P4494. Of these people, 5.358 have been identified from mass graves and 648 from surface remains. We know that the total figure is a conservative one, since not all human remains have been exhumed, examined, matched, or even located. The vast majority of the 5.358 identified from graves have been identified via DNA from primary and secondary mass graves connected to the major execution sites of Kozluk, Branjevo Farm, Pilica Dom, Petkovci Dam, Orahovac, as well as Kravica and surroundings. With respect to the Kozluk sites, primary and secondary graves, currently a total of 1.040 victims have been identified via DNA analysis from the graves related to the Kozluk sites. This is without counting the 14 victims identified from the Kozluk surface remains of whom 12 were reported as missing from Potocari. Additionally, an anthropological minimal number of individuals, MNI, estimate of 400 persons, has come out as a result of last year's exhumation of the Cancari 4 and the Cancari 6 secondary graves, which should be confirmed by future DNA identifications. And, finally, we should keep in mind that we do not yet have the DNA results or MNI estimates for the Cancari 1 grave related to the Kozluk exhumations, to the Kozluk execution site, which is Cancari 1 is scheduled for exhumation in the course of this year. With respect to the Branjevo Farm, Pilica Dom-related primary and secondary graves, currently there is a total of 960 victims who have been identified via DNA from related graves. In addition, there is an anthropological MNI, minimum number of individuals, estimate of 84 people for Cancari 8 secondary grave, which was exhumed last and which Mr. Janc has testified is related to Branjevo Farm execution. From Petkovci Dam, currently 805 victims have been identified via DNA analysis from graves related to this execution site. With respect to Orahovac, currently 807 persons have been identified from the graves related to this execution site. Finally, from Kravica, currently 1.319 [realtime transcript read in error "1.309"] victims have been identified via DNA analysis from the graves which are related primarily to the Kravica site. As discussed in the Prosecution final brief at paragraph 1087, as well as in the Janc corrigendum, Exhibit P4492, and in his testimony at references 33518 to 33520, 33527, and from 33638, approximately over 100 individuals buried in the Kravica-related graves are not from Kravica. While it may never be possible to identify the precise number of those individuals who are not from Kravica, Janc's explanation in testimony, cited above, as well as the testimony of the two Kravica survivors, that the respective rooms they were placed in in the Kravica warehouse were filled to the brim - this would be Witness PW-156 at transcripts T-094 to T-0 -- 7095, and PW-111 at transcript reference 6690 - taken together with Exhibit P4529, which is the declaration of Investigator Blasczyk regarding the Kravica warehouse measurements, show that approximately 500 men could fill up each of these two rooms in the warehouse. Therefore, it is the Prosecution's position, also cited at paragraph 1987 of its final brief, that a minimum of 1.000 individuals were brought to the Kravica warehouse prior to the executions and that they were executed there. In addition to the current number of 1319 individuals who have been identified, there will likely be more identifications related to the Kravica execution site coming from last year's exhumations of the Zeleni Jadar 1A and Zeleni Jadar 1B graves. Further references -- specific references to the related graves can be found in Dusan Janc's report, Annex A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Ms. Soljan, but at one point at page 75, line 1, it's 1.309, and you just mentioned 1319.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Indeed, it should be 1.319 individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, in addition to these almost 5.000 individuals, and the exact number is 4.931 individuals coming from these graves, and I just want to point out to you the exact location in Annex A where the listing of all these graves is located, this would be at ERN XO19-4271 to XO19-4272 of Annex A of Mr. Janc's report, which is P4490. Now, in addition to this total of 4.931 individuals found in these graves, from these mass executions, we also have an additional 4.013 individuals found in graves which were either primary undisturbed graves, mass graves which were previously known to the ICTY, such as Cerska -- sorry, this would be 413 individuals who are found, then, in undisturbed mass graves previously known to the ICTY, such as Cerska, Nova Kasaba 96 and 99, Sandici, Konjevic Polje, and Trnovo, as well as smaller individual and other graves, which include Bisina, Motovska Kosa, Brezjak, Potocari, and others. All of which are listed in Dusan Janc's report. Your Honours, taking into account the fact that there are currently 5.358 men who have been identified from graves, mass graves, that there is an estimated minimum number of individuals of approximately 500 persons which were recovered last year from the Cancari -- from the three Cancari graves, Cancari 4, 6, and 8, taking into account that there is, as of yet, an unknown number of other individuals who are recovered last year from the Zeleni Jadar 1A and 1B graves, as well as with the knowledge that there are new exhumations taking place this year, including that of the Cancari 1 secondary mass grave, as well as that there are continuing identifications still arriving from previously exhumed graves, there is no question that at least 6.000 but most likely more Srebrenica individuals who are either separated at Potocari or who surrendered and were captured from the forest, were buried inside mass graves as well as smaller or individual graves. With respect to the surface remains, Your Honours, we know that since 1996 957 cases of surface remains were collected, of which 648 have been identified via DNA identification. We know from Annex B of Mr. Janc's report that the vast majority of these surface remains identified individuals, and the precise number is 538, were located in the Pobudje area, the area just before the Konjevic Polje crossing. While with respect to many of the surface remains identifications, we may never know what happened, at least with respect to two locations, Nezuk and Snagovo, we have evidence that executions took place along the column route. This means that not all surface remains represent battle casualties, but, on the contrary, that they represent victims of executions. In addition to the testimony we have from the Snagovo survivor, Witness PW-106, about the execution which took place at Snagovo, we also have ICMP's identification of one of the individuals mentioned by PW-106, and we can find his name at Exhibit P4491, the confidential annex to the Janc report, under case ID SNA-16, at ERN page R065-7769. With respect to the Nezuk execution, in addition to the testimony of the two survivors, the surface remains of one of the five individuals mentioned by the survivors has been located as a surface remain at Tisova Kosa. We can find information on him under case ID TIS-1 at Exhibit P4491, ERN R065-7766. We also have a few combat reports which show that there were other instances of executions similar to those taking place at Nezuk and Snagovo using words such as "liquidation," "neutralising," to describe the killing of captured Bosnian Muslim men from the Srebrenica enclave by VRS and MUP personnel through July and August. We have seen, for example, the 14 July 1995 regular combat report by the 5th Engineering Battalion deputy commander, Mila Simanic - this Exhibit P2672, in which he states that: "About 1.000 to 1.500 enemy civilians and soldiers were arrested and killed." When asked about why he had exclaimed, "God forbid," upon being presented with this combat report during his previous interview with the OTP, Simanic testified that in his view, "this --" I quote "... constitutes a crime." This is at transcript reference T-14641. We also have seen the 19 July 1995 Zvornik Public Security Centre report to the MUP office of the minister, which states, and I quote: "Eight Muslim soldiers were neutralised. We learned from them that some 200 Muslims, armed with automatic and hunting rifles, are located in a sector below the old road near Snagovo." This is Exhibit P4486. It is obvious from the wording of this report that the men must first have been captured, then interrogated, and finally euphemistically neutralised. Finally, let us recall the Rogatica Brigade's regular combat report of 8 August 1995, in which the Rogatica Brigade Commander Rajko Kusic, reports that five balijas from Zepa were liquidated. This is at Exhibit P209. This report also stated, and I quote: "The same day, in the vicinity of Luka, an unarmed Ustasha, born in Srebrenica, 24 years old, was liquidated. Before he died, he said that he fell behind the others and he was looking for food." This man was alive when he was captured, and he was murdered with the full knowledge and authorisation of Rajko Kusic, the Rogatica Brigade commander. In addition to the evidence of these types of illegal killings, which are actually reflected in writing, we may never know how many individuals walking in the column may also have been killed by Ljubomir Borovcanin's anti-aircraft guns as they were being called down to surrender. Now, there is no evidence, as the Defence argues, that between 1.500 to 3.000 individuals died as a result of legitimate combat. This is argued in Popovic brief at paragraph 708, in the Beara final brief at 583 to 586. There is also no evidence that that proximity of Srebrenica-related graves to the column route means legitimate combat casualties were buried there. This is from Beara's final brief at paras 634 to 635. There is no evidence of combat taking place in the rear of the Zvornik Brigade zone of responsibility at the time of the Branjevo Farm, the Kozluk, the Petkovci Dam and the Orahovac executions. There is also no evidence of combat taking place either in the area of Glogova or Ravnice, let alone Zeleni Jadar, Budak, Bljeceva, there is, however, plenty of evidence described in detail in section 3(e) of the Prosecution final brief concerning the separation of numerous men at Potocari, about their surrender or capture from the column on the 13th of July, about their placement on buses or trucks, about their transportation to various holding areas in Bratunac, in Kravica, in the Zvornik area of responsibility, Zvornik Brigade area of responsibility, and, finally, plenty of evidence about their ultimate executions. Forensic evidence, survivor testimony, as well as intercept and other evidence show that individuals found in graves in the Zvornik Brigade area of responsibility, as well as in other areas such as Trnovo and Bisina, were killed at those sites, not elsewhere. Evidence also shows that machinery for the excavation of the Orahovac, Petkovci dam, Kozluk and Branjevo farm mass graves, was mobilised to be there contemporaneously with the mass execution or immediately thereafter. Again, this evidence can be found at section 3(e) of the Prosecution final brief, as well as at paragraphs 1080 to 1104 of the forensic connection between graves section, and paragraphs 1155 to 1174 on forensic DNA and demographic evidence. Finally, to suggest that the Bosnian Serb Army would exhume legitimate battle casualties two months after combat in the dead of night and relocate these bodies to isolated, well-hidden areas is implausible, to say the least. Just to address a couple of specific points made in the Defence final briefs, there is no support for the conclusion in the Beara Defence brief at paragraphs 614 to 616, as well as 636, that individuals found in the Glogova and Zeleni Jadar graves must have died in combat, given findings of shrapnel and grenades. Ample forensic evidence has been presenting [sic], Your Honours, including the Hadley report, Exhibit P4525, the US NCIS Kravica report, Exhibit P678, the Baraybar report on Zeleni Jadar, P2576, the testimonies of Jean-Rene Ruez reference page 1468 and 1469 to 1471, as well as Manning at 18978 to 18983. We also have the testimony of survivors and those present in the area during the Kravica warehouse killings that grenades were being lobbed into the Kravica warehouse during the execution. We have seen photos and a video of grenade handles and fly-off levers found outside the Kravica warehouse. The reference to that video is Exhibit P1575. Therefore, the individuals located in Kravica-related graves, as a matter of fact, would show signs of shrapnel injury. There is no evidence concerning the fact that bodies of victims from 1992 and 1993 are buried in Srebrenica-related graves, as the Popovic Defence claims at paragraph 716. The Popovic Defence cites the testimony of Witness PW-161 to argue that bodies of Muslim men who died in 1992 are also buried in the Glogova grave. However, this is a misstatement of Witness PW-161's evidence. While PW-161 acknowledged that he was involved in the burial of 100 to 150 Muslim men in 1992, he clearly stated that these bodies were buried some 10 to 12 kilometres from Glogova. The reference to for this is 9398 at line 14. He further stated, and I quote: "I went to the Glogova locality with Mr. Ruez, but I never told him that in 1992 Muslim bodies had been buried in Glogova, because after Glogova I took Mr. Ruez to the locality where the 100 to 150 Muslim bodies had been buried in 1992." This is at 9399, lines 6 to 10. There is also no evidence that bodies from 1992 and 1993 were counted as part of the ICMP's DNA identification count, as the Popovic Defence claims at paragraph 713. The Popovic Defence refers specifically to the Bljeceva 1 grave, stating that, I quote: "Forty-six persons were identified, of which six remains were not Srebrenica-related." Noting that these remains, these six remains, were from 1992. Similarly, the Nikolic brief, at paragraph 1451, criticises the figure -- the overall figure of the 5.358 individuals identified in graves because, among other reasons, and I quote: "The Bljeceva grave also contains remains of approximately 50 individuals who died in 1992-related events ." This makes it sound as though Mr. Janc counted these six or 50 bodies of individuals who died in 1992, when he was counting Srebrenica-related ICMP DNA identification. The record is clear, however, Your Honours, that Mr. Janc, in his count, did not count victims unrelated to the fall of Srebrenica. We see this at transcript 33509, 33513, as well as in his exhibit, the report -- his report, the Exhibit P4490. In fact, Mr. Janc was at pains to explain why he did not count the nine unique unnamed DNA profiles for Bljeceva, as well as one unique unnamed DNA profile from Lipje [phoen] precisely because of the possibility -- or, rather, the impossibility of connecting them to Srebrenica-related information for the time being. This can be found at transcript reference 33508 to 33509. The 46 individuals currently identified as Srebrenica missing from the Bljeceva 1 grave are individuals who report to the ICMP as missing following the fall of Srebrenica in July 1995. These are the only individuals counted by Mr. Janc for the Bljeceva grave. Finally, at paragraph 1451 of their brief, the Nikolic Defence also argues that this current number of 5.358 individuals identified from Srebrenica-related graves is incorrect because: (a), an exact number of individuals connected to the Kravica execution site cannot be provided and, (b), and I'm paraphrasing, because there is evidence that 12 individuals found in the Cerska grave were alive after July 13, 1995, the date of the execution as alleged in the indictment, and were reported as being seen as late as 17 July 1995. Your Honours, neither of these reasons affects the actual figure or the number of individuals affected -- identified from each of the exhumed graves. With respect to Kravica, it is clear that 1.319 individuals have been identified, regardless of whether they were executed at Kravica, the Vuk Karadzic school, in Grave L or elsewhere. Similarly, the fact that individuals found in the Cerska grave may have been reported as being captured or at least as reported as last being seen on 16 or 17 July changes nothing about the number of bodies identified from this grave. In fact, the ICMP data actually under-reports the number of individuals for this grave, rendering the figure 5358 a conservative one; namely, in this instance we know from Dr. Haglund's report on the Cerska exhumation, Exhibit P611, that because it is an undisturbed primary grave, that there are 150 complete bodies which were exhumed from this grave. At this time, we have only 142 ICMP DNA identifications coming from this grave. In conclusion on this topic, Your Honours, evidence shows that thousands of separated, captured, surrendered Bosnian Muslim men and boys from Srebrenica were systematically executed in July 1995, that they were buried in mass graves, in many cases reburied, but some of them also left out, becoming surface remains. The Prosecution submits that a minimum of 5.358 men identified from graves, but actually closer to 6.000 men when counting the already known 500 estimated minimum number of individuals from last year's exhumations, are all victims of executions. The Prosecution also submits that not all of the 648 men identified from the surface were killed in legitimate combat, by suicide, land-mine, or by friendly-fire. This, for the time being, leaves us with approximately a thousand to 1500 individuals we currently have no identification information on. Some of them might not be discovered because they are lying in graves, without survivors, or because their bones are shattered in such small pieces inside secondary graves that no DNA can be obtained. However, Your Honours, new exhumations, new DNA identifications, continue to take place, and as they continue to come to light, the tragic story of murder of more than 7.000 Muslim men and boys will only serve to underline the gravity of the crimes committed against them and against the Bosnian Muslim population of Eastern Bosnia. Turning very briefly to the second issue, Your Honours, that of the destruction of women and children, the Popovic Defence, at paragraph 643 of its final brief, states that, I quote: "The Prosecution did not prove that the movement of the Muslim population from Srebrenica to the BiH-held territory disabled their normal life and reproduction. Namely, there is no normal living at the time of war." Similarly, at paragraph 644, the Popovic Defence, and I quote: "... rejects charges for genocide toward women and children. Events occurred in Potocari after the fall of Srebrenica toward women and children did not have significant impact to their capability to reproduce and did not at all jeopardise the survival of the protected group." Your Honours, the Prosecution has dealt in detail with the issue of the destruction of women and children in its final brief at paragraphs 1105 through 1128 as well as with the legal aspects of the charge of genocide at paragraphs 2806 to 2834 and will therefore not repeat the discussion here. However, I will briefly make the following point: We have read and heard evidence concerning impact of the forcible transfer on the population of Srebrenica and Zepa, as well as the separation and murders of the men, which caused incalculable suffering and permanent damage to the tens of thousands of living survivors who have been consigned to a lifetime of physical/mental suffering. The women and children have been traumatised by the events of July 1995. There has been a breakdown of family life, since thousands of men have disappeared. There exists the possibility that many of the survivors may never know who happened to the loved ones who went missing. Many have spoken of the pre-war life that was reasonably prosperous, relatively care-free, under the guidance, protection, and leadership of their husbands and fathers. Now that life has changed, and they have been living in abject poverty in many cases, forced to take on responsibilities not normally taken on by the female members of the Bosnian Muslim population of Eastern Bosnia. What once were vibrant communities are no more. The accused, originally from the Eastern Bosnia area or employed there, knew well about the importance of men in the traditional patriarchal societal structure of Bosnian Muslims of Eastern Bosnia. We talk about this at paragraph 1126 and 1127 of the final brief. Their crimes were deliberately inflicted, resulting in the death of thousands of Muslim men and boys. We have evidence from countless witnesses who have lost multiple male members -- male members of their families, some of whom have lost not only their loved ones, but also realise that their family name will disappear, since no men remain to carry it forward. Your Honours, the words that truly bring home the enormity of the tragedy, the abnormality of life, the destruction experienced by those who lost their family members and their old way of life, was cited to by Chief Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte at the opening of this case at lines 377 -- or pages 377 to 378. They are the words of Witness PW-121, a woman who last saw her husband and older son as they joined other men to head off into the woods as Srebrenica fell and whose youngest son, barely 14 years old, had been violently torn from her in Potocari. At the time this witness testified, she did not know about the fate of her husband and sons, and when asked what she thought may have happened to them, she responded in an anguished cry. I will not take up the Court's time today with a video-clip of her testimony, though if you would like to read it, it is at Exhibit number P2266, transcript pages 5761, especially lines 15 to 22. This woman was a classic example of somebody suffering from the so-called "Srebrenica syndrome," living a life on hold, waiting, uncertain about the fate of her loved ones, hoping against hope that they may be alive, unable to move on with her life until finding out for sure, a classic example of destruction, of failure to live normally, of serious mental harm caused to a Srebrenica woman. Could we go into private session for a moment, please, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that. Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it, Ms. Soljan, we didn't hear that witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, she was a 92 bis witness, and we have her testimony. This is Exhibit P2266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: 2226. And to conclude, Your Honours, while it may be true that as the Popovic Defence says, there is no normal living at the time of war, the point here is that since July 1995, there has been no normal living for the tens of thousands of survivors of Srebrenica and Zepa. The story of Witness PW-121 is just one of many thousands of tragic stories we've heard from those who have survived the horror of separations, the forcible transfers, the loss of loved ones, of property, into small but now tragically well-known enclaves of Eastern Bosnia. Thanks to the advent of DNA matching, some women and children of Srebrenica and Zepa have finally, over time, begun learning about the fates of their missing men after years of not knowing. However, many tragically still live without knowing, and some perhaps will never know and will never be able to move on and lead a normal life. This concludes my submission, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Soljan. Now, Mr. McCloskey, I think you're the one left, and we also have 10 minutes left. Do you want to start now, or shall we continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would greatly appreciate if we could start tomorrow, but I can guarantee you I will be finished by the second period. I don't intend to take more than two hours, perhaps less, though it's hard to say. And I'm also ready to answer questions or receive any homework that you might have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, all right. So, Mr. Zivanovic, I suppose you will go first after the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are put on notice that you will be expected to start tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, you are put on notice you may have to start tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
